scope: Scope v2 review before registration; no performance grid was run.
mathematical_findings: The active-subsolution lower-bound theorem is sound for a valid Bellman subsolution and an optimized dummy-root coupling.
For fixed active set A and baseline h, the global LP root optimum equals backward DP with inactive nodes clamped to h.
All-active equality is equality of the root optimum; a root-only LP need not return the exact value at every table entry.
The fixed-depth future-marginal sum of one-time OT costs is a Bellman subsolution for absolute cost and squared cost when squared-cost terms use W2 squared units.
decisive_objections: The global LP itself supplies no tighter root bound than the cheaper same-A same-h clamped recursion.
Partial-state admissible-heuristic DP and occupation-prioritized expansion have close AO/LAO-star prior art; novelty is not established.
Exact-optimal occupation can miss inactive alternatives selected by the lower problem; a deterministic H=2 fixture gives exact 1 but lower 0.25 for absolute cost and 0.03125 for squared cost.
Current work counts omit dense h, mask, table-copy, stage-cost and verification work; the upper policy and outward numerical witness are not yet part of the API.
required_action: Do not register the current global-LP claim. Retain the proved future-marginal subsolution and clamped recursion as components. Formulate a new hypothesis around a deployable root-lower-policy frontier activation rule, with complete work accounting and a direct LAO-star/clamped-DP comparison.
not_inferred: No impossibility for active-set, global-dual, certified or tree algorithms.
No conclusion from distinct optimal vertices, failed occupation headroom or measured 1/w scaling.
